newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel shares end little changed in heavy trading.
newsitem.headline: Israel shares end little changed in heavy trading.

text.p: Israeli shares closed almost unchanged on Thursday after sharp swings amid heavy trading dominated by Maof options speculators, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 0.07 percent, or 0.18 points, to 242.95 on all-share turnover of 164 million shekels against 70 million shekels on Wednesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.02 percent higher at 250.88.

"The session opened with lots of activity by options speculators. The Maof players succeeded in pushing the Maof downwards to 248 in the Meretz," said Yossi Weidelfeld at Eyal Securities. "After the expiry of the contracts the market rose again closing almost unchanged."
The Meretz is the preliminary computerised session in which heavy capitalisation shares are traded in the morning.
A trader at Bank Leumi said the main reason for the recovery after the Meretz session was heavy purchasing of United Mizrahi Bank.
"Overall the market is expected to remain stable in the near future as investors wait for fresh news," the trader said.
Clal Industries lost 0.25 percent to 1,576 agorot. Yossie Rosen said on Thursday he was resigning as managing director of the company after less than four months on the job.

Clal Israel, Clal Industries parent, closed unchanged at 90.5 agorot. The company said on Thursday that net profit fell in 1996 to 111.6 million shekels from 203.7 million shekels in 1995 after posting a 1.3 million shekel loss in the final quarter.

The most active shares were Bank Hapoalim, which fell 1.0 percent to 648 agorot on turnover of 12.0 million shekels; Bank Leumi, which lost 0.5 percent to 536 agorot on volume of 11.7 million shekels; and Bezeq Israel Telecom, which rose 3.5 percent to 898 agorot on turnover of 11.3 million shekels.
